items.text: US shoppers spent about $7.1B online on Thanksgiving, +10.4% and above Adobe's $6.9B forecast. Adobe expects a record $12.9B for Black Friday and $15.1B on Cyber Monday. $ADBE $AMZN $SHOP

Black Friday session winners and losers: $SNDK closes +16% and $MU +7.6% as memory leads; $XP +18% on Brazil's new finance minister. Losers: $ALVO -12.4% (court blocks biosimilar launch), $VRTX -5.2% (FDA delay).
Closing bell, Black Friday half-day: Nasdaq +2.3%, S&P 500 +1.6%, Dow +1.2% as AI and chip stocks rebound. All three indexes finish the holiday week higher, led by the Dow.
$AMZN up about 3.8% on strong Black Friday demand; $WMT edges higher as the first holiday-shopping data comes in.
Buyers return into the half-day close: at 12:20 p.m. ET the S&P 500 is +1.3% and the Dow +1%, with $MU up nearly 7% while $NVDA stays slightly red.
$IQMX +19% after winning an order to install a 54-qubit quantum computer at a South Korean data center.
$VERA +16.5%: the FDA's delay on rival $VRTX's IgA nephropathy drug gives Vera's own kidney drug more room in the race.
Why Brazil stocks are ripping: Brazilian assets jumped after the country named a new finance minister, per Bloomberg. $BBD, $PBR and $ABEV are among the day's big US-listed gainers.
Gold up about 2.8% to $3,636 an ounce, bouncing off its weakest level in over a year as the AI sell-off calms. $GLD $GDX
Bitcoin drops below $59,000 after the US open, giving back a morning move above $62,000. Crypto stocks like $COIN and $MSTR trade with it.
$NVDA flips red (-1.4%) after a 4% premarket gain, lagging the AI rebound after a report that it halted some exports to Southeast Asia. $ANT +8.4%, $TSLA +4.7%, $PLTR +3.7% at the same time.
The opening pop fades: by 10:20 a.m. ET the S&P 500 is +0.7%, Dow +0.6%, Nasdaq +0.8%, roughly half the gains from the bell, in thin holiday trading.
$COIN +4% after Wedbush starts covering the fintech sector.
Why $NVDA lags: per the FT, it told partners like $DELL and $SMCI to freeze AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, a route Chinese firms used to rent restricted compute.
$COHR +12%, one of the day's biggest chip-sector gainers as optical and memory names bounce; $MU +6%, $AMD +2.4%.
$ANT +4% early, $META and $AMZN +2% each, $AVGO almost +2% as the rally pares to Dow +0.6% in the first half hour.
Opening bell: Dow +507 points (+1%), S&P 500 +1.2%, Nasdaq +1.5% as tech leads the post-Thanksgiving rebound. The Dow came into Friday up 5% this week, on pace for its best week since April 2025.
Optical and storage names lead S&P 500 premarket gainers after a brutal month: $LITE +8% to $514.50 (still down 48% in a month), $WDC +6.2%, with $COHR and $STX also near the top.

$SPCX +4% premarket after Musk said on X he will donate another SpaceX share to every kid in America every year, on top of the one-share-per-Trump-Account pledge. The stock is still about 12% lower over the past month.
Silver rips: $SLV +7.1% premarket, pulling miners with it: $CDE +7%, $KGC +5.8%, $FCX +5.5%, $SCCO +5%.
$TSM +3.3% premarket to about $353 as new Counterpoint data puts its share of the global foundry market at 75%, driven by AI chip demand.
China's chipmakers post their biggest one-day gains ever as Beijing calls in its state-backed "national team" buyers. In US premarket: China STAR 50 chip ETF $KSTR +12.6%, $BILI +7.3%, $NIO +4.8%.
$SNDK +11% premarket, one of the strongest names as memory stocks lead the AI rebound after Thanksgiving.
Brazil ADRs jump after Thursday's Ibovespa rally: $BBD +18%, $VALE +8.8% premarket.
$QFIN +4% after a Q3 beat: adjusted EPS $0.51 per ADS vs $0.46 expected, even as revenue fell 37% from a year ago.
$ALVO -10%: a US court temporarily blocked the launch of its biosimilar AVT05 in a patent fight with J&J's Janssen; Q3 revenue also missed. The company will appeal.
AI cloud renters bounce hardest: $NBIS +9.5%, $CRWV +7.9% premarket.
$MRVL +7.3% premarket after beating fiscal Q3 expectations. The stock had lost about 43% over the past month.
$VRTX -7.3% premarket: the FDA extended its review of kidney drug povetacicept by up to three months; the decision is now due by Feb. 28, 2027 instead of Nov. 30.
Chip stocks lead the premarket rebound: $AMD +7%, $MU +6%, $NVDA +4.7%, $AVGO +4.7%, $INTC +4.5%. $NVDA is still more than 37% below its October record.
Nasdaq 100 futures +2.5%, S&P 500 +1.9%, Dow +1.4% as Wall Street returns from Thanksgiving for a half-day session that closes at 1 p.m. ET.
Oil climbs near monthly highs on supply worries: WTI +2.6% to $85.80, Brent $97.27.
